records.name: BougeRV CR 23QT 12V Portable Fridge Freezer (22 L, single compartment, -7 to 50 °F, 12/24 V DC + AC)
specs: 23 qt (22 L, 0.78 cu ft), one compartment
-7 to 50 °F (-22 to 10 °C) per BougeRV's spec table
Compressor cooling; compressor maker not stated by BougeRV
MAX mode 60 W, ECO mode 45 W (BougeRV spec table)
12/24 V DC car cord and 100-240 V AC adapter, both included
3-stage vehicle-battery monitor; cut-off voltages not stated on BougeRV's product page
22.7 x 12.6 x 13.0 in outside, 13.8 x 9.8 x 9.8 in inside; 21.16 lb
8.3 W steady-state DC draw, 48.9 W while cooling to 35 °F, 3.0 °F average display error, lowest reading -3.2 °F, 19.8 lb measured
records.warranty: BougeRV gives portable fridges a 2-year warranty from the date of purchase covering defects in materials, workmanship and performance, with the product page listing 2 years for this model.
records.returns: BougeRV accepts returns within 30 days of receipt if the item is new, undamaged and unmodified, after contacting support first; the buyer pays return shipping unless the item arrived defective or wrong (policy at https://www.bougerv.com/policies/refund-policy).
records.summary: A small single-compartment 12 V compressor fridge that runs from a car's 12/24 V socket or a wall outlet and can be set anywhere from -7 to 50 °F. In OutdoorGearLab's test it held temperature on about 8 W of steady DC draw, though its display read about 3 °F off the measured temperature.
records.fit: Suits one or two people on day trips, weekend car camping or a road-trip seat-side fridge, where a 23-can interior is enough and no app control is needed.
caveats: OutdoorGearLab's sample reached -3.2 °F from a 75 °F start, short of the advertised -7 °F floor, and its display averaged 3.0 °F off the measured temperature.
OutdoorGearLab lists interior condensation and DC power cord issues as reasons to avoid it.
BougeRV's page gives conflicting ECO-mode figures (45 W in the spec table, under 36 W in the FAQ) and its FAQ calls the unit dual-zone although it has one compartment.

No app or Bluetooth control (BougeRV lists App: N), and the 'Fridge+Battery' bundle uses a separate 266 Wh power station that BougeRV says runs a portable fridge for about 6 hours, not a built-in battery.

records.summary: A single-zone 30-quart compressor fridge with a slot for BougeRV's detachable 240 Wh LiFePO4 battery, so it can run away from the car and recharge from solar, USB-C or its AC adapter. It cools to -4 °F and is controlled from the panel or BougeRV's app.

caveats: No independent measured test of the CRX3 was found; older BougeRV 30-quart reviews cover earlier models with a different -7 to 50 °F range.
BougeRV does not give a runtime on the 240 Wh battery for this fridge.
BougeRV's figures conflict: noise is ≤35 dB on the page but 45 dB in the manual, and ECO mode is 45 W in the comparison table but 'below 35W' in the page copy.
The listed 23.8 lb weight is not marked as with or without the battery, and the battery is only included in the 'Fridge+Battery' and solar-kit variants.
The manual says mode adjustment is possible only through the BougeRV app.

records.warranty: BougeRV lists 10 years on materials and workmanship and a 30-year linear power-output warranty for this panel, honored for the original buyer on purchases from bougerv.com with proof of purchase, with the buyer prepaying shipping to BougeRV.

records.summary: A 200-watt rigid roof panel with N-type TOPCon cells and 24 bypass diodes, which BougeRV says keeps up to 85% of output when part of the panel is shaded. Its 36.4 V open-circuit voltage and 15 A fuse rating are aimed at RV, van and off-grid systems run through a charge controller.
records.fit: Suits RV, van or camper owners mounting a fixed panel on a roof where vents, racks or trees shade part of it during the day. BougeRV's FAQ says it works with 12 V and 24 V battery systems through a suitable charge controller.
caveats: The 85% partial-shade figure is BougeRV's own claim; no independent shade test of this panel was found.
BougeRV's FAQ expects 150–170 W in real use, not the 200 W rating.
At 23.4 lb and 1.2 in thick it is a framed rigid panel, not for curved surfaces or carrying around.
BougeRV's product page does not state the connector type, cable length, frame material, mounting-hole layout or certifications (not stated by BougeRV).

The power-output warranty on the product page (30 years) is longer than the general term in BougeRV's warranty policy table (25 years performance, 5–10 years materials by series); the policy says to check the manual for each series.

Materials and workmanship coverage is 5 years, half the 10 years BougeRV lists for its rigid ShadePower 200W.

records.name: BougeRV 5kW Portable Diesel Heater (2026, 110V/12V), 5 L tank, app and LCD control, stainless shell
specs: 5 L; 9–27 h per tank by heat setting (BougeRV launch release)
12 V in the spec table; title and description say dual 110V/12V power
150 W at start-up (12 A while igniting); 10–60 W running (5–6 A)
Up to 3,000 m (9,842 ft), automatic adjustment
22 lb (10 kg); 15.3 × 9.7 × 12.4 in; 304 stainless steel shell
BougeRV app (up to 33 ft) or LCD panel; IPX4 control panel
Overheat shutoff, short-circuit, reverse-connection and over-voltage protection; separate combustion and heated-air paths with exhaust vented outside
records.warranty: BougeRV lists a 2-year warranty on this heater, honored for the original buyer on purchases from bougerv.com with proof of purchase, with repair preferred over replacement and the buyer prepaying shipping to BougeRV.
records.returns: BougeRV's product page lists a 30-day guarantee, and its refund policy accepts returns within 30 days of receipt if the item is new, undamaged and unmodified, after contacting BougeRV first, with the buyer paying return shipping unless the product arrived defective or wrong.
records.summary: An all-in-one 5 kW diesel heater with its 5 L tank, burner and controls in one stainless-steel body; it sits outside and blows heated air through a hose into a tent, van, garage or workshop while the exhaust stays outside. It needs electricity for ignition and the fan, drawing up to 150 W at start-up and 10–60 W while running.
records.fit: Suits winter campers, ice fishers and garage or shop users who want ducted heat from a unit that stays outdoors, with power from a 12 V battery or power station or, per BougeRV, a 110 V outlet. Buyers who only need 12 V can compare BougeRV's earlier 12 V Portable Diesel Outdoor Heater (GG001-TIUSCA), listed at $199.99 on bougerv.com when read on 2026-11-21.
caveats: BougeRV recommends using the diesel heater outdoors; its product page and launch release give no ventilation or carbon-monoxide guidance and list no CO sensor (not stated by BougeRV), even though the description names home, garage and RV use, so a separate CO alarm in the heated space is the buyer's call.
BougeRV says the exhaust muffler reaches 482°F (250°C) at 77°F ambient and must not be touched or covered with anything flammable.
An exhaust pipe extension is not included and is sold separately; BougeRV does not list the box contents (not stated by BougeRV).
It needs power to start and run: BougeRV says a power station's 12 V DC port must support a 15 A+ peak, and the spec table lists only 12 V although the title says 110V/12V.

No independent measurements were found; Bob Vila's hands-on review (Glenda Taylor, 2026-01-19) of a BougeRV portable diesel heater, not identified as this 110V/12V version, gives no measured figures and reports that the household power adapter received did not work while 12 V did.
